audit.why: 52.03% over 1499 games — the largest sample in Ambessa's top-lane table. Left untouched.

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Graves level 6 and Ambessa the two-item stage — both are backwards against the page's own prose. The text calls 6 'where it tilts to you' and 'your first real flip onto a kiter', then says two items 'slides back to a coinflip and Graves can reclaim it'.
audit.why: Public Execution is a 1250-unit blink plus suppression — the single cleanest answer to a dash-and-reset marksman, so 6 is Ambessa's. At two items Graves has bruiser resists on top of True Grit and Ambessa's damage is entirely physical, so the duel tilts back to him.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Graves / Skill / Ambessa / Ambessa / Ambessa / Ambessa / Graves in both layers — 4-2-1 to Ambessa, which fits 52.03%. Difficulty stays early-and-late weighted with a wide mid-lane window.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes were keyed to an invented mechanic ('Smoke Screen's blind') and to Ambessa having 'flat armor-pen shred' on her R, which is nowhere in Riot's text for Public Execution.
audit.why: Public Execution is blink-to-farthest-champion, suppress, slam for damage and a stun — no penetration. Graves's real spike structure is Quickdraw at 3 (16s, and his basic attacks keep lowering it), Smoke Screen's long 26s rank-1 cooldown shortening to 18s at rank 5, and True Grit doubling on a forward dash.
audit.corrected: Spikes rewritten to: levels 1-2 (his spread, and the minion-block counterplay), level 6 (1250-unit blink, 130s R), first item (Q at 10s inside a 22s Smoke Screen gap), and his own two-item window when a forward Quickdraw doubles his resists.

audit.whatIsWrong: The single most-repeated claim on this page is wrong. Smoke Screen is described five times as blinding your empowered auto. Riot's text for Smoke Screen is: a smoke cloud that reduces sight range, with magic damage and a brief slow on the initial impact. It is a nearsight and a slow, not a blind — your autos still connect. The page also says Collateral Damage's 'backward knockback can break your dash-into-auto chain', and the only knockback in Riot's Graves text is his passive knocking back non-champions.
audit.why: The distinction decides how you fight him. Against a blind you must wait it out before committing an empowered auto. Against a nearsight you can keep attacking — the problem is that you lose sight of him and eat a slow, so he breaks the chase rather than the trade. Two verified interactions were also missing entirely: New Destiny fires 4 bullets that cannot pass through units, so a melee minion between you eats most of a spread; and Quickdraw dashed toward a champion grants two stacks of True Grit instead of one, meaning his resists double at the exact moment he commits at you.
audit.corrected: Every 'blind' rewritten as nearsight-plus-slow with the 26/24/22/20/18s cooldown. Minion-blocking added to whys[0], spikes[0] and early. Two-stack True Grit added to whys[6], spikes[3] and the two-item phase. The R knockback claim removed rather than restated.

audit.whatIsWrong: Trading advice treated Quickdraw as a fixed timer you can wait out.
audit.why: Quickdraw is 16/15/14/13/12s, but hitting enemies with basic attacks lowers its cooldown and refreshes the resist boost. Farming a wave puts it back up early, so 'wait for his E' is only true if he is not attacking anything.
audit.corrected: Stated in whys[1], early and breakdown.cooldowns — his autos shave the cooldown, so bait it rather than count it down.

audit.whatIsWrong: The most punishable cooldown in this lane was never named with a number.
audit.why: Smoke Screen at rank 1 is 26 seconds — by far the longest cooldown either laner has before ultimates. That is the window where a kiting marksman has no disengage and Ambessa's dash chain simply reaches him.
audit.corrected: 26/24/22/20/18s stated in mid, late and breakdown.cooldowns; the first-item spike is now keyed to the 22s gap.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[2] justified Plated Steelcaps by claiming 'his pellet autos, Q and ult are all physical'.
audit.why: Riot's text gives no damage type for End of the Line or Collateral Damage, and Smoke Screen is explicitly magic damage — so the blanket claim is not supported. The boots are still right, but for the auto-attack reduction against his shotgun.
audit.corrected: Reworded to justify Steelcaps on the shotgun spread alone.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page mentions that Graves's shotgun is minion-blockable, which is the entire level 1-3 counterplay.
audit.why: New Destiny: 'Attacks fire 4 bullets, which cannot pass through units.' Standing so a melee minion is between you and Graves means most of the spread lands on the minion. For a melee champion who has to walk into 425-ish range to do anything, that is the difference between a losable and an unlosable early lane.
audit.corrected: Added to whys[0], spikes[0].text and early.

edits.before: Graves owns the very first levels — a point-blank pellet spread plus an End of the Line Q simply out-damages your one ability before your Medarda combo comes online, so don't step into his shotgun range to grab a single CS. The trick is his Quickdraw: it's both his escape and his armor stacker, so the instant you commit E for the slow he wants to dash out. Land that E slow first — it's a near-total decaying slow — then your passive Drakehound's Step dash sticks to him for the empowered auto and Q2 follow-up. If Quickdraw is on cooldown, that's your green light to all-in.
edits.after: Graves owns the very first levels — a point-blank pellet spread plus an End of the Line Q simply out-damages your one ability before your Medarda combo comes online, so don't step into his shotgun range to grab a single CS. New Destiny fires 4 bullets that stop on the first unit they hit, so last-hit with a melee minion between you and most of the spread never reaches you. Quickdraw is both his escape and his resist stacker, so land Lacerate's slow first, then Drakehound's Step sticks for the empowered auto and Sundering Slam.

edits.before: This is where it tilts to you. At 6 Public Execution is the answer to a kiter: it blinks you behind the farthest target in the line, suppresses through his Quickdraw, and crashes him down stunned — he can't just dash and reload anymore. Pair it with E-slow into W (brace his pellet burst with Repudiation to amp your next output) and your Q1-auto-Q2 chunks half his bar while R's flat armor-pen shreds his stacked armor and heals you on every ability hit. The one thing that saves him is Smoke Screen — it blinds your empowered auto — so bait it or go in once it's down.
edits.after: This is where it tilts to you. At 6 Public Execution is the answer to a kiter: it blinks up to 1250 units to the farthest champion in the line, suppresses through his Quickdraw, and slams him down stunned — he can't just dash and reload anymore. Pair it with Lacerate's slow into Repudiation, bracing his pellet burst so the blocked damage amps your slam, and Q1-auto-Q2 chunks half his bar. What saves him is Smoke Screen on 26/24/22s: it nearsights you and slows on impact, so he breaks the chase inside it. Bait it or go once it's spent.

edits.before: Past two items it slides back to a coinflip and Graves can reclaim it. He builds bruiser-tanky for a marksman, so your physical-only damage running into Quickdraw's armor plus his item armor starts to bounce, and Collateral Damage's backward knockback can shove you out of a dash chain mid-combo. Smoke Screen up blinds your one big empowered auto in the fight. Your edge is still the R flip — if you can blink-suppress him onto your team before he kites, you win the skirmish; if he gets the Smoke + ult spacing right, he kites you out. Close it on your first-item spike rather than betting on the late brawl.
edits.after: Past two items it slides back to Graves and he can reclaim the lane. He builds bruiser-tanky for a marksman, and a Quickdraw dashed toward you grants two stacks of True Grit instead of one, so his armour and MR double at the exact moment your physical-only burst arrives — and his basic attacks keep shaving that 16s cooldown back down. Smoke Screen every 18s at rank 5 nearsights you and slows on impact, which is enough to break a chase in the open. Your edge is still the R flip — blink-suppress him onto your team before he resets spacing and you win the skirmish. Close it on your first-item spike.

notes: The 'Smoke Screen blinds you' claim appears across the whole Ambessa page set and is wrong — Riot's text is a sight-range reduction plus a brief slow on impact. Worth sweeping every champion's Graves matchup for it, not just Ambessa's. Unverified and therefore removed rather than restated: Collateral Damage having a backward knockback that displaces the target (Riot's only knockback text for Graves is his passive knocking back non-champions), End of the Line and Collateral Damage being physical damage, and Lacerate's slow being 'near-total decaying'. Also note champ-data/_kits/graves.json carries a 'terrain: creates terrain, blocks paths and dashes' flag on End of the Line; Riot's description says the shell detonates on colliding with terrain, so the flag is a parse misfire and I did not use it. Same Ambessa-wide problem as the Gragas file: an 'R flat armor-pen shred' and 'heals you on every ability hit' are asserted here and appear in neither Public Execution's nor Drakehound's Step's Riot text.
